title: Set 106

sentences.ko: 오늘 내가 뭘 했는지는 묻지 마. 콘크리트 진입로를 어떻게 까는지 처음부터 끝까지 설명할 수 있는데, 아빠한테 전화는 아직도 안 했어. 이게 다 경기 점수 좀 보려고 앉았다가 시작된 거야. 그런데 웃긴 건, 우리 집엔 진입로도 없어.
sentences.text: Don't ask me what I got done today. I can tell you exactly how a concrete driveway gets poured, start to finish, and I still haven't called my dad back. This all started because I sat down to check the score. And here's the thing, I don't even have a driveway.

alts.text: You really don't want to know what I got done today. I could walk you through pouring a concrete driveway, start to finish, and I still haven't called my dad back. It all kicked off because I sat down to check the score. And the best part? I don't even have a driveway.

I would rather you not ask what I accomplished today. I can explain to you precisely how a concrete driveway is poured, from beginning to end, and I still have not returned my father's call. All of this began because I sat down to check the score. The remarkable part is that I do not even have a driveway.

sentences.note: **start to finish** 는 처음부터 끝까지 빠짐없이 전부라는 뜻입니다. **here's the thing** 은 정작 중요한 대목이나 어이없는 대목을 꺼낼 때 붙이는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 유튜브 보다가 시간 다 날린 얘기

sentences.ko: 그 금요일은 휴가를 못 내. 팀에 누가 벌써 그 주를 통째로 신청해 놨거든. 그러면 그냥 퇴근하고 차로 올라가는 건 어때? 저녁은 날리겠지만 토요일은 하루가 다 남잖아. 네가 비행기가 낫다면 어떻게든 맞춰 볼게. 어느 쪽이든 이달 말까지는 회사에 말해야 해.
sentences.text: I can't get that Friday off, because somebody on my team already put in for the whole week, so what if we just drive up after work instead? We'd lose the evening but we'd still have all of Saturday. If you'd rather fly I'll make it work, I just have to tell them by the end of the month either way.

alts.text: That Friday's not happening, somebody on my team already claimed the whole week, so how about we just drive up after work? We'd lose the evening but Saturday would still be all ours. If you'd rather fly I'll make it work, I just gotta tell them by the end of the month either way.

I am unable to take that Friday off, as someone on my team has already requested the entire week, so could we drive up after work instead? We would lose the evening, but we would still have all of Saturday. If you would prefer to fly, I will make it work; in either case, I simply need to inform them by the end of the month.

sentences.note: **put in for** 는 휴가나 자리를 미리 신청해 둔다는 말입니다. **I'll make it work** 는 어떻게든 되게 해 보겠다는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 이 일이 싫은 것도 아니야. 그게 아내한테 설명이 안 되는 부분이고. 3월에 회사에서 나를 승진에서 건너뛰었는데 나는 사람들한테 괜찮다고 했어. 그때부터 계속 그 자리가 다시 돌아오려면 몇 년을 더 버텨야 하나 계산만 하고 있어. 그래서 채용 공고를 하루 종일 탭에 띄워 놓고는 한 군데도 지원을 안 했어.
sentences.text: I don't even hate the job, which is the part I can't explain to my wife. They passed me over back in March and I told everybody I was fine with it, and ever since then I've been doing the math on how many more years I'd have to put in before it comes around again. So I keep the listings open in a tab all day and I haven't applied to a single one.

alts.text: The job's not even bad, and that's the part I can't explain to my wife. They passed me over back in March and I told everybody I was fine with it, and ever since then I've been counting up how many more years I'd have to put in before it comes around again. So I've got the listings open in a tab all day and I still haven't applied to any of them.

I do not even dislike the job, which is the part I cannot explain to my wife. I was passed over in March and I told everyone that I was fine with it, and ever since then I have been calculating how many more years I would have to put in before it comes around again. So I keep the listings open in a tab all day, and I have not applied to a single one.

sentences.note: **passed me over** 는 승진 대상에서 나를 건너뛰었다는 말입니다. **doing the math** 는 숫자를 따져 본다, 계산해 본다는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 이거 미친 소리인지 좀 말해 줘. 여기 내는 돈이면 마당 있는 집에서 살 수 있어. 근데 한 시간 반을 나가야 하고, 이 도시에서 내가 아는 사람은 다 회사에서 만났거나 우리 동네에서 만난 사람들이야. 그러니까 돈은 아끼는 대신 길에 갇혀 있고 아는 사람도 없는 거지. 그런데 또 밤 열두 시에 안 자고 그 집 세 채를 또 보고 있어. 마음 한쪽은 확실히 가고 싶은 거야.
sentences.text: Okay, tell me if this is crazy. I could have a house with a yard for what I'm paying here, but it's an hour and a half out, and everybody I know in this city I met through work or on my own block. So I'd be saving money just to sit in traffic and not know anybody. But then I'm up at midnight looking at the same three houses again, so part of me clearly wants it.

alts.text: Alright, how nuts does this sound? For what I'm paying here I could have a house with a yard, but it's an hour and a half out, and everybody I know in this city I met through work or on my own block. So I'd be saving money just to sit in traffic and know nobody. But then I'm up at midnight looking at the same three houses again, so part of me clearly wants it.

All right, please tell me whether this is unreasonable. I could have a house with a yard for what I am paying here, but it is an hour and a half away, and everyone I know in this city I met through work or on my own block. So I would be saving money only to sit in traffic and know no one. And yet I am awake at midnight looking at the same three houses again, so some part of me evidently wants it.

sentences.note: **for what I'm paying here** 는 지금 여기 내는 돈이면 이라는 뜻으로 값을 견줄 때 씁니다. **part of me** 는 내 마음 한구석은 이라는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 솔직한 답을 원해, 듣기 좋은 답을 원해? 몸에는 아주 잘 맞아. 근데 너답지가 않아. 내 생각엔 두 번 입고 나면 저 의자 위에 계속 얹혀 있을 것 같아. 아직 택 안 뗐으면 반품하고 아까 먼저 입어 본 수수한 걸로 사. 그거 입었을 때는 얼굴이 환해졌거든. 이건 거울도 안 봤잖아.
sentences.text: Do you want the real answer or the nice one? Because it fits you great, it's just not you, and I think you're going to wear it twice and then it lives on that chair. If you still have the tag, take it back and get the plain one you tried on first. You lit up in that one. With this one you didn't even look in the mirror.

alts.text: Honest answer or nice answer? Because the fit is great, it's just not you, and I'm telling you, you'll wear it twice and then it lives on that chair. If you've still got the tag, take it back and grab the plain one you tried on first. You lit up in that one. This one, you didn't even look in the mirror.

Would you like the honest answer or the kind one? It fits you very well; it simply is not you, and I suspect that you will wear it twice and then it will live on that chair. If you still have the tag, return it and get the plain one you tried on first. You lit up in that one. In this one, you did not even look in the mirror.

sentences.note: **it's just not you** 는 옷이 나쁜 게 아니라 그 사람 분위기와 안 맞는다는 말입니다. **lit up** 은 표정이 환하게 밝아졌다는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 친구가 산 옷 어떠냐고 물었을 때 솔직하게 말하기

reviewed: 1번 한국어: "점수 좀 확인하려고"는 무슨 점수인지 안 잡힌다. check the score 는 경기 중계 점수를 본다는 말이라 "경기 점수 좀 보려고"로 고쳤다.
3번 한국어: "다들한테"가 어색하고 승진에서 건너뛴 주체가 빠져 있어서 "회사에서 나를 승진에서 건너뛰었는데", "사람들한테"로 고쳤다.
3번 casual: "haven't applied to one of them"은 한 군데도 안 했다는 뜻으로 잘 안 읽힌다. "still haven't applied to any of them"으로 바꿨다.
2번 formal: "might we drive up"은 너무 옛말투라 말투만 올린 것이 아니게 된다. "could we drive up"으로 바꿨다.
